title: The software supply chain: where it breaks

videos.script: Here is an uncomfortable fact. In the worst supply chain attacks of recent years, the code the victims reviewed was fine. {{fine}} The problem was somewhere else. In a build server. In a script downloaded on every run. In a tag that somebody moved. In a package that changed hands. {{where}} This lesson draws the chain, from a person's change to the software that runs, and names each link with SLSA's letters. {{chain}} Then it places seven real incidents on that chain. SolarWinds, Codecov, event-stream, xz, and three more. Each one comes with the control that would have caught it. {{incidents}} And you try two of those controls on your own machine. pip refuses a file whose hash changed by one byte. And two package indexes show you that the higher version wins, whoever published it. {{hands}} By the end, you can look at any control and say which link it protects. And which links nothing protects yet. {{map}}
